suggestions.explanation: The function repeatedly polls the filesystem every 500ms using setTimeout recursion for up to 15 seconds, which is wasteful when fs.watch could react immediately when the port file is created.

suggestions.location: ensureServerRunning and pollForPortFile functions in out/server.js
suggestions.explanation: Multiple synchronous fs calls (fs.readFileSync, fs.existsSync, fs.unlinkSync) are used throughout the server startup path, blocking the Node.js event loop while performing I/O operations that have async equivalents.

suggestions.location: onDidSaveTextDocument handler / debounceTimer in activate function in extension.js
suggestions.explanation: A nested setTimeout inside another setTimeout creates a timer-based polling-like pattern where a status bar item is shown after 30 seconds and then disposed after another 30 seconds, creating unnecessary timer overhead and a poor UX delay instead of reacting promptly.

Repeatedly polling the filesystem every 500ms with setTimeout to check for a port file is wasteful; a fs.watch or chokidar watcher would react instantly when the file appears instead of burning CPU cycles on timed checks.

Using synchronous fs.existsSync and fs.readFileSync blocks the Node.js event loop on every poll iteration and during startup, preventing other async tasks from executing while disk I/O completes; these should be replaced with fs.promises.access and fs.promises.readFile.

Calling fs.existsSync and fs.readFileSync inside an async function blocks the event loop unnecessarily, negating the benefits of the async signature and stalling VS Code's extension host thread during file reads.
